intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 (MRT37) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ANK3 gene.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 (MRT37) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ANK3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems, we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: Homozygous ANK3 mutation in a consanguineous family with ID; the MRT37 designation is OMIM nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 (MRT37) is a neurodevelopmental disorder marked by moderate intellectual disability, an attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)-like phenotype, and behavioral problems. It was described in a consanguineous family carrying a homozygous truncating mutation that affects the longest isoform of ANK3 (Iqbal et al., 2013).

checks.evidence_quote: illustrate the genetic and molecular relation between a wide range of neurodevelopmental disorders
checks.explanation: Abstract frames the phenotypes as neurodevelopmental disorders.

paragraphs.text: Iqbal et al. (2013) reported a consanguineous family in which several members had moderate intellectual disability, an ADHD-like phenotype, and behavioral problems. Affected family members also had severe behavioral problems.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) reported a consanguineous family in which several members had moderate intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a consanguineous family with moderate ID.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family reported by Iqbal et al. (2013) had an ADHD-like phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the family had an ADHD-like phenotype.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family reported by Iqbal et al. (2013) had severe behavioral problems.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions 'behavioral problems' but does not call them severe. Only a later citing paper (Fang et al., 2023) uses the word 'severe'.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of MRT37 in the consanguineous family reported by Iqbal et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of MRT37 in the consanguineous family reported by Iqbal et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems, we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation
checks.explanation: A homozygous mutation in a consanguineous family directly implies autosomal recessive transmission.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability, an ADHD-like phenotype, and behavioral problems, Iqbal et al. (2013) identified a homozygous single-basepair truncating frameshift mutation in the ANK3 gene. The mutation affected only the longest ANK3 isoform. Iqbal et al. (2013) described it as the first familial ANK3 mutation reported. A Drosophila knockdown model showed memory defects, which supported a causal role for the mutation.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) identified a homozygous mutation in the ANK3 gene in affected members of a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability, an ADHD-like phenotype, and behavioral problems.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems, we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The ANK3 mutation identified by Iqbal et al. (2013) is a single-basepair truncating frameshift mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms a truncating frameshift but does not say it is a single-basepair change. That detail comes only from a later citing paper (Fujitani et al.).

checks.claim: The ANK3 frameshift mutation identified by Iqbal et al. (2013) affected only the longest ANK3 isoform.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: The mutation lies in the longest isoform, in contrast with the translocation case, where all isoforms were disrupted.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) described their ANK3 frameshift mutation as the first familial ANK3 mutation reported.
checks.evidence_quote: which represents the first reported familial mutation in the ANK3 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: A Drosophila knockdown model of the ANK3 ortholog showed memory defects.
checks.evidence_quote: The causality of ANK3 mutations in the two families and the role of the gene in cognitive function were supported by memory defects in a Drosophila knockdown model.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports memory defects in a Drosophila knockdown model.

checks.claim: The memory defects in the Drosophila knockdown model supported a causal role for the ANK3 frameshift mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The causality of ANK3 mutations in the two families and the role of the gene in cognitive function were supported by memory defects in a Drosophila knockdown model.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the knockdown results supported causality of the ANK3 mutations.

paragraphs.text: In the same report, Iqbal et al. (2013) described an unrelated patient with borderline intelligence, severe ADHD, autism, and sleeping problems. In this patient, a balanced translocation disrupted all isoforms of the ANK3 gene.

checks.evidence_quote: In a patient with a borderline intelligence, severe attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism and sleeping problems
checks.explanation: The abstract refers to 'the two families', so this patient is unrelated to the consanguineous family.

paragraphs.text: Iqbal et al. (2013) found that knockdown of the ANK3 ortholog in Drosophila caused memory defects. They took this as support for a role of ANK3 in cognitive function.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) took the memory defects in Drosophila ANK3-ortholog knockdown as support for a role of ANK3 in cognitive function.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with MRT37, Iqbal et al. (2013) identified a homozygous single-basepair truncating frameshift mutation in the ANK3 gene. The mutation affected only the longest isoform. A Drosophila knockdown model showed memory defects, which supported a causal role for the mutation.
